topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: These opening remarks introduce the lecturer, outline the cancer lecture series, and establish the learning objectives regarding cancer causation and carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Origins of Cancer: Intrinsic Errors, Genetics, and Environmental Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the multifactorial drivers of cancer development, comparing intrinsic replicative mutations, inherited predispositions, and geographic epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Carcinogenic Agents and Mutagenic Mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine specific infectious, physical, and chemical agents alongside the biochemical mechanisms through which they induce direct or metabolically activated DNA damage.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammation, and Host Cell Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the non-mutagenic processes that facilitate cancer development, highlighting the initiator-promoter paradigm, inflammatory microenvironments, and life-stage tissue vulnerability.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting and Testing Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the analytical and experimental strategies used to detect carcinogen exposure and evaluate carcinogenic risk, spanning genomic signatures, epidemiology, animal bioassays, and in vitro tests.
